info.title: idto Verification API
info.description:
idto is an identity and KYC verification platform. This API lets you run PAN, Aadhaar, bank account,
business/GST, vehicle, mobile, employment, credit-bureau, DigiLocker, driving-licence, face-match,
liveness, document-OCR, address and eSign verifications through a single set of HTTP endpoints,
either individually or composed into a workflow on the idto dashboard.

## Response envelope (v2)

Every product under `/v2/verify/*` shares one response contract. A 2xx HTTP response always carries
`status: "success"` and `billed: true`, whether the result is a full match (`error_code: null`,
`data` populated) or a definitive no-record outcome (`error_code` set to an `IDTO_2xx` code,
`data: null`). Callers distinguish a full match from a no-record result by checking `error_code`,
never by inspecting `status`: there is no `"failed"` status anywhere in the v2 API.

A raised error (any non-2xx response) always carries `status: "error"`, `data: null`, `billed: false`,
and the legacy string flags `chargeble: "false"` and `user_consent: "false"` alongside `billed: false`.
Raised errors are never billed, with exactly one exception: `IDTO_204` (no readable Aadhaar QR found)
is a raised, non-2xx error that is still guaranteed `billed: false` like every other raised error. It
is called out in the error table below because it is the one product-specific error most integrators
ask about by name, not because its billing behavior differs from any other raised error.

## v1 vs v2

`/v2/verify/*` is the current, vendor-agnostic contract described above, used for every product that
has been migrated onto it. `/verify/*` (no `/v2` prefix) remains live for products that have not been
ported yet. Because v1 predates the shared envelope, each v1 product's response shape is its own:
consult that product's schema and examples rather than assuming the v2 envelope applies.

## Idempotency

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (max 255 characters) on any v2 request to make retries safe. If the
same key is replayed with an identical request body, the original result is returned without re-running
the verification or billing again. If the same key is replayed with a **different** body, the request
is rejected with `IDTO_010` (422). A request with the same key that is still in flight returns `IDTO_004` (409). The header is optional; omitting it runs every request as new.

## Authentication

Every request to `/verify/*` and `/v2/verify/*` must include two headers: `X-Client-ID` and
`X-API-Key`. Both are issued per environment (staging and production credentials are separate and
not interchangeable).

## Error Codes

| Code | HTTP | Message |
|---|---|---|
| IDTO_001 | 400 or 422 | Invalid input. Please check the request and try again. |
| IDTO_004 | 409 | Duplicate request. Verification ID already exists. |
| IDTO_005 | 400 | User consent is required to proceed. |
| IDTO_006 | 429 | Too many requests. Please wait a moment and retry. |
| IDTO_007 | 500 | Verification could not be completed due to a service configuration issue. Please contact support at tech@idto.ai. |
| IDTO_008 | 503 | The verification service is momentarily busy. Please retry shortly. |
| IDTO_009 | 402 | Insufficient credits or balance. Please recharge and try again. |
| IDTO_010 | 422 | Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body. |
| IDTO_101 | 400 | A required parameter is missing from the request. |
| IDTO_102 | 400 | A required parameter is missing from the request. |
| IDTO_103 | 503 | This verification could not be completed. Please retry shortly or contact support at tech@idto.ai. |
| IDTO_201 | 200 | Bank account is invalid or does not exist. |
| IDTO_202 | 200 | Record is invalid or does not exist. (per-product messages may override this text) |
| IDTO_203 | 202 | Verification is still in progress. Retrieve the result using reference_id. |
| IDTO_204 | 422 | No readable Aadhaar QR was found in the image. (NOT billed, the sole zero-cost raised-error carve-out) |
| IDTO_205 | 422 | Invalid OTP or session expired. Please request a new OTP. |
| IDTO_206 | 429 | Maximum OTP attempts exceeded. Please generate a new OTP. |
| IDTO_207 | 404 | No result found for this reference_id. |
| IDTO_401 | 400 | The account number provided is invalid. |
| IDTO_402 | 400 | The IFSC code provided is invalid. |
| IDTO_403 | 503 | This verification could not be completed. Please retry shortly or contact support at tech@idto.ai. |
| IDTO_503 | 413 | The image could not be processed. Please try a clearer, smaller image. |
| IDTO_509 | 500 | Face match could not be completed. Please try again. |
| IDTO_609 | 500 | Liveness could not be determined. Please try again. |

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Webhook configuration for asynchronous result delivery.

## What gets delivered

Two kinds of event are delivered by webhook: a verification-link session completing (see the
Verification Links tag), and an eSign docket finishing signing (see the eSign tag). Both use the
same delivery, signing and retry mechanism described below, but the two payload shapes are
different and are not wrapped in any shared envelope.

## Signing scheme

The request body sent to your `webhook_url` is compact, key-sorted JSON, produced the same way as
Python's `json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)`, and sent as raw UTF-8 bytes.
A Unix timestamp (whole seconds, encoded as a string) is generated at send time.

The string that gets signed is built by concatenating, as bytes: the timestamp string, a literal
`.`, then the raw request body bytes. In Python terms this is `f"{timestamp}.".encode() + raw_body_bytes`,
a bytes concatenation, not a string concatenation of the decoded body. The signature is
`HMAC-SHA256(secret, signing_string)`, hex-encoded.

Every delivery carries three headers:

- `X-idto-Event-Id`: a unique id for this specific delivery, used to de-duplicate retried or
  re-sent events on your side.
- `X-idto-Timestamp`: the same timestamp string used when building the signature.
- `X-idto-Signature`: the signature in the form `sha256=<hex signature>`.

To verify a delivery, recompute the HMAC over `timestamp + "." + raw_body_bytes` using your stored
secret, and compare the result to `X-idto-Signature` with a constant-time comparison, never a plain
`==` on the strings. During a secret rotation, deliveries in flight may be signed with either the
previous secret or the new one for a short grace window, so verify against both secrets if you have
just rotated.

## Event payloads

There is no shared `event` wrapper key across both event types, so distinguish them by shape: the
eSign event carries an explicit `event` field, the session-completion event does not.

Session completion (implicit, no `event` field):

```json
{
  "session_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-467e-bd93-4a2c11e0a1b2",
  "session_token": "sess_3c9a1e2b7d4f5061",
  "status": "completed",
  "outcome": "approved",
  "partial": false,
  "completed_steps": ["mobile_verification", "pan_validation", "face_match"],
  "skipped_steps": [],
  "fallback_steps": [],
  "branch_excluded_steps": [],
  "consents": [
    {"type": "data_processing", "version": "1.0", "timestamp": "2026-09-14T10:15:30Z"}
  ],
  "event_id": "evt_5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c",
  "report": {
    "url": "https://reports.idto.ai/r/8f14e45f-ceea-467e-bd93-4a2c11e0a1b2?sig=...",
    "expires_at": "2026-09-14T11:15:30Z",
    "content_type": "application/pdf",
    "filename": "report.pdf"
  }
}
```

The `report` key is only present when a PDF report is attached to the session and the merchant has
report attachment enabled. Its `url` is a fresh, short-lived presigned link generated for that one
delivery, never a permanent link.

eSign completion:

```json
{
  "event": "esign.completed",
  "event_id": "evt_esign_2a3b4c5d6e7f8091",
  "tranx_id": "b6e1f2a0-1234-4abc-9def-0123456789ab",
  "docket_id": "b6e1f2a0-1234-4abc-9def-0123456789ab",
  "document_id": "doc_1a2b3c4d5e6f7081",
  "signing_status": "signed",
  "signed_at": "2026-09-14T10:15:30Z"
}
```

No document bytes are included in this event. Retrieve the signed PDF separately through the eSign
document-download endpoint documented elsewhere in this spec.

## Delivery and retries

A delivery is attempted up to 5 times with exponential backoff between attempts, starting at
roughly 10 seconds and doubling on each retry, capped at 1 hour between tries. If every attempt is
exhausted, the delivery is marked permanently failed and is not retried again. Events created before a signing secret exists are still attempted: they run through this same 5-attempt retry cycle and are permanently dead-lettered within a few minutes, the same as any other delivery failure. There is no separate holding queue that waits for you to configure a secret. Generate one with `POST /merchant/webhook-config/rotate-secret` before, or immediately after, setting a webhook URL, or the earliest events from that window are lost for good.

parameters.description: Make retries of this exact request safe. post.description:
Confirms that a bank account exists and can receive money, and returns the name registered on it. A valid account returns `error_code: null` with `data`. An invalid, closed or non-existent account returns HTTP 200 with `error_code: "IDTO_202"` and `data: null`. Both are billed. Any other failure is a non-2xx error and is never billed.

When you do not send an `Idempotency-Key`, IDTO still blocks a second identical request (same body) while the first is running: the second gets `IDTO_004` (409). Once the first finishes, an identical request runs again and is billed again. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to have retries replay the stored result instead.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional, at most 255 characters, scoped to your account. Replaying a key with the same body returns the stored result of the first call without running or billing again (kept for 48 hours). The same key with a different body returns `IDTO_010` (422). The same key while the first call is still running returns `IDTO_004` (409). If the first call returned an error, nothing is stored and a retry runs again. Without this header, identical concurrent requests are still blocked with `IDTO_004`.

account_number.description: Account number, 6 to 40 letters or digits, no spaces or symbols.

ifsc.description: IFSC of the account's branch: 4 letters, a zero, then 6 letters or digits. Case-insensitive. Also accepted as `ifsc_code`.

name.description: Optional. The name you expect on the account. The response carries no match result for it, so compare it with `data.account_holder_name` yourself.

reference_id.description: Optional. Your own reference for this check, 1 to 40 letters, digits or hyphens.

user_id.description: Optional. Your identifier for the end user, stored with the call.

workflow_session_token.description: Optional. Set only when this call runs inside an IDTO workflow session. If that session is priced per workflow, the call is free and `billed` is `false`.
